question: How many engines does the DA 42 NG have, and what is the engine designation?

options.text: One Austro Engine E4-C engine with twin turbochargers

explanation: AFM 2.4(b)-(c) lists the number of engines as 2 and the engine designation as E4-C, manufactured by Austro Engine.

question: What is the maximum take-off RPM (shown as propeller RPM) for the DA 42 NG?
explanation: AFM 2.4(d) lists both maximum take-off and maximum continuous RPM as 2300 RPM.

question: What is the maximum permitted propeller overspeed, and for how long?

options.text: 2500 RPM for a maximum of 5 minutes
2600 RPM for a maximum of 20 seconds
2500 RPM for a maximum of 20 seconds
2400 RPM for a maximum of 10 seconds

explanation: AFM 2.4(d) lists the maximum overspeed as 2500 RPM, limited to 20 seconds.

question: What is the maximum take-off power for one engine, and for how long may it be used?
explanation: AFM 2.4(e) gives maximum take-off power as 100% (123.5 kW), limited to 5 minutes.

question: What is the maximum continuous power per engine?
explanation: AFM 2.4(e) states maximum continuous power is 92%, equal to 114 kW.

question: What is the minimum oil pressure at or above 1500 RPM?
explanation: AFM 2.4(f) sets the minimum oil pressure at 2.5 bar for RPM at or above 1500; below 1500 RPM the minimum is only 0.9 bar.

question: What is the minimum oil pressure allowed below 1500 RPM?
explanation: AFM 2.4(f): below 1500 RPM the minimum oil pressure is 0.9 bar, rising to 2.5 bar at or above 1500 RPM.

question: What is the maximum oil pressure?
explanation: AFM 2.4(f) gives a maximum oil pressure of 6.5 bar, with a normal range of 2.5 to 6 bar.

question: What is the engine oil quantity range?
explanation: AFM 2.4(g) gives an oil quantity of 5.0 to 7.0 liters, with maximum oil consumption of 0.1 liter/hr.

question: What is the maximum permitted oil consumption?
explanation: AFM 2.4(g) states maximum oil consumption of 0.1 liter/hr.

question: What is the maximum engine oil temperature?
explanation: AFM 2.4(h): oil temperature maximum is 140 °C, with a normal range of 50 to 135 °C.

question: What is the normal range for engine oil temperature?
explanation: AFM 2.4(h) gives the normal (green) oil temperature range as 50 °C to 135 °C, with the red maximum at 140 °C.

question: What is the maximum gearbox temperature?
explanation: AFM 2.4(i) lists a maximum gearbox temperature of 120 °C; the minimum is -30 °C, rising to 35 °C required for full load.

question: What is the minimum gearbox temperature required for full load operation?
explanation: AFM 2.4(i) requires a minimum gearbox temperature of 35 °C before full load may be applied; the absolute minimum is -30 °C.

question: Is there a cautionary (yellow) gearbox temperature range imposed by the engine manufacturer?

options.text: Yes — the yellow range is a hard maximum imposed by Austro Engine
No — the gearbox temperature has no upper limit at all
No — the yellow range on the G1000 is added only to alert the pilot ahead of the 120 °C limit, with no specific time limit
Yes — a 5-minute time limit applies in the yellow gearbox range

explanation: A note under AFM 2.4(i) explains the cautionary gearbox range exists only because of the lag between power changes and gearbox temperature; it carries no specific time limit.

question: What is the maximum coolant temperature?
explanation: AFM 2.4(j): coolant temperature maximum is 105 °C; the minimum required for full load is 60 °C, and the absolute minimum at start-up is -30 °C.

question: What minimum coolant temperature is required before full load may be applied?
explanation: AFM 2.4(j) requires the coolant to reach a minimum of 60 °C before full load; the minimum at start-up is only -30 °C.

question: What is the fuel temperature limitation?
explanation: AFM 2.4(k) and 2.16.1 both give the fuel temperature range as -30 °C to 60 °C (-22 °F to 140 °F).

question: What is the fuel pressure limitation?
explanation: AFM 2.4(l) gives fuel pressure limits of 4 to 7 bar. A note adds that fuel pressure itself is not indicated on the G1000 — only a low-pressure warning is shown.

question: Is fuel pressure directly displayed on the G1000?

options.text: Yes — fuel pressure in bar is shown on the engine page at all times
Yes, but only on the MFD system page, never on the PFD
No — fuel pressure can only be checked by maintenance on the ground
No — only a fuel pressure warning illuminates if pressure drops below the limit

explanation: A note under AFM 2.4(l) states fuel pressure is not indicated on the G1000; a warning illuminates only if pressure falls below the limit.

question: What is the electrical system voltage limitation?
explanation: AFM 2.4(m) gives voltage limits of 24.1 V to 32.0 V for the 28 V DC system.

question: What is the maximum alternator amperage?
explanation: AFM 2.4(n) sets the maximum amperage at 70 A; the L/R ALTN AMPS warning triggers above this value.

question: What is the propeller diameter of the DA 42 NG?
explanation: AFM 2.4(q) gives the mt-Propeller MTV-6-R-C-F / CF 190-69 a diameter of 190 cm.

question: What is the propeller blade pitch angle in the feathered position?
explanation: AFM 2.4(r) gives the feathered pitch angle as 80° ± 1° (measured at 0.75 R); the low-pitch angle is 13° ± 0.2°.

question: What is the propeller low-pitch blade angle (at 0.75 R)?
explanation: AFM 2.4(r) states the low-pitch angle is 13° ± 0.2° at 0.75 R; feathered position is 80° ± 1°.

question: What is the maximum restart altitude for an immediate engine restart, if MÄM 42-938 is NOT installed?
explanation: AFM 2.4(w): without MÄM 42-938, the maximum restart altitude for an immediate restart is 18,000 ft; restarts within two minutes are limited to 10,000 ft. With MÄM 42-938 installed, immediate restarts are limited to 15,000 ft instead, with an OAT-dependent table applying up to 10,000 ft.

question: If MÄM 42-938 (engine software VC33_2_05_19 or later) IS installed, what is the maximum altitude for an immediate engine restart?
explanation: AFM 2.4(w): with MÄM 42-938 installed, immediate restarts are limited to 15,000 ft pressure altitude (down from the 18,000 ft that applies without the modification), with a further OAT-based maximum engine-off time table applying up to 10,000 ft.

question: With MÄM 42-938 installed, up to 10,000 ft pressure altitude, what is the maximum permitted engine-off time when the OAT is below -15 °C?
explanation: The AFM 2.4(w) table (applicable with MÄM 42-938) allows only 2 minutes engine-off time below -15 °C OAT, rising to 5 minutes between -15 °C and -5 °C, and 10 minutes above -5 °C.

question: What is the maximum restart airspeed using the starter?

options.text: 100 KIAS, or the airspeed for a stationary propeller, whichever is lower
125 KIAS, or the airspeed for a stationary propeller, whichever is lower
100 KIAS fixed, regardless of propeller state

explanation: AFM 2.4(x) gives the starter restart airspeed limit as max. 100 KIAS or the airspeed for a stationary propeller, whichever is lower — the starter must never be engaged on a windmilling propeller.

question: What is the airspeed range for a windmilling engine restart?
explanation: AFM 2.4(x) limits a windmilling restart to between 125 and 145 KIAS — below 125 the propeller may not windmill continuously, and above 145 a restart can overspeed the propeller.

question: Below what altitude, and above what altitude, is intentional engine shutdown prohibited?

options.text: Below 3,000 ft AGL, and above 18,000 ft pressure altitude
Below 5,000 ft AGL, and above 10,000 ft pressure altitude
Below 3,000 ft AGL, and above 10,000 ft pressure altitude
Below 1,000 ft AGL, and above 18,000 ft pressure altitude

explanation: AFM 2.4(y) prohibits intentional engine shutdown below 3,000 ft AGL and above 10,000 ft pressure altitude.

question: What is vMCA (minimum control speed, airborne) with flaps UP?
explanation: AFM 2.2 gives vMCA as 71 KIAS with flaps UP and 68 KIAS with flaps APP.

question: What is vMCA (minimum control speed, airborne) with flaps in the APP position?
explanation: AFM 2.2: vMCA is 68 KIAS with flaps APP, and 71 KIAS with flaps UP.

question: What is vYSE, the best rate-of-climb speed with one engine inoperative?
explanation: AFM 3.1.2 and the airspeed indicator markings give vYSE as 85 KIAS, marked by the blue radial.

question: What is vNE (never exceed speed) for the DA 42 NG?
explanation: AFM 2.2 gives vNE as 188 KIAS — also the limit for gear extended (vLE) and gear extension (vLOE).

question: What is vNO, the maximum structural cruising speed?
explanation: AFM 2.2 gives vNO as 151 KIAS — above this speed, only smooth air and caution are permitted.

question: What is the maximum landing gear extended speed (vLE)?
explanation: AFM 2.2: vLE and vLOE (extension) are both 188 KIAS; vLOR (retraction) is lower, at 152 KIAS.

question: What is the maximum landing gear operating speed for retraction (vLOR)?
explanation: AFM 2.2 gives vLOR as 152 KIAS, lower than the 188 KIAS permitted for extension (vLOE) or with the gear already extended (vLE).

question: What is the maximum flaps-extended speed with flaps in the LDG position?
explanation: AFM 2.2 gives vFE as 113 KIAS for LDG flaps and 133 KIAS for APP flaps.

question: What is the maximum flaps-extended speed with flaps in the APP position?
explanation: AFM 2.2 gives vFE as 133 KIAS for APP flaps and 113 KIAS for LDG flaps.

question: What is the operating maneuvering speed vO above 1800 kg (3968 lb)?
explanation: AFM 2.2 stages vO by weight: 112 KIAS up to 1700 kg, 119 KIAS from 1700-1800 kg, and 122 KIAS above 1800 kg.

question: What is the operating maneuvering speed vO up to 1700 kg (3748 lb)?
explanation: AFM 2.2: vO is 112 KIAS up to 1700 kg, rising to 119 KIAS between 1700-1800 kg and 122 KIAS above 1800 kg.

question: On the airspeed indicator, what does the blue radial line mark?

options.text: Best angle of climb speed (77 KIAS)
Best rate of climb speed, single engine (85 KIAS)
Minimum control speed, single engine (71 KIAS)

explanation: AFM 2.3: the blue radial marks vYSE = 85 KIAS; the red radial at 71 KIAS marks vMCA (single-engine minimum control speed), and the red radial at 188 KIAS marks vNE.

question: On the airspeed indicator, what does the lower red radial line (at 71 KIAS) mark?

options.text: Best rate of climb speed, single engine

explanation: AFM 2.3 marks 71 KIAS with a red radial for vMCA — the single-engine minimum control speed; the blue radial at 85 KIAS is vYSE.

question: What is the white arc airspeed range (flaps fully extended operating range) if MÄM 42-678 is NOT carried out?
explanation: AFM 2.3: without MÄM 42-678 the white arc is 62-113 KIAS; with MÄM 42-678 it becomes 64-113 KIAS.

question: What is the green arc (normal operating range) on the airspeed indicator if MÄM 42-678 is carried out?
explanation: AFM 2.3: with MÄM 42-678 carried out, the green arc becomes 72-151 KIAS instead of the standard 68-151 KIAS.

question: What is the maximum take-off mass WITHOUT MÄM 42-678 installed?
explanation: AFM 2.7 gives the baseline maximum take-off mass as 1900 kg; this rises to 1999 kg only if MÄM 42-678 is carried out.

question: What is the maximum take-off mass WITH MÄM 42-678 installed?
explanation: AFM 2.7: MÄM 42-678 raises the maximum take-off mass from the baseline 1900 kg to 1999 kg.

question: What is the minimum flight mass of the DA 42 NG?
explanation: AFM 2.7 lists the minimum flight mass as 1450 kg.

question: What is the maximum zero fuel mass WITHOUT MÄM 42-659 installed?
explanation: AFM 2.7: the baseline maximum zero fuel mass is 1765 kg, rising to 1835 kg if MÄM 42-659 is carried out.

question: What is the maximum zero fuel mass WITH MÄM 42-659 installed?
explanation: AFM 2.7: MÄM 42-659 raises the maximum zero fuel mass from 1765 kg to 1835 kg.

question: What is the maximum landing mass WITHOUT MÄM 42-659 installed?
explanation: AFM 2.7: the baseline maximum landing mass is 1805 kg; with MÄM 42-659 carried out it rises to 1999 kg.

question: What is the maximum landing mass WITH MÄM 42-659 installed?
explanation: AFM 2.7: MÄM 42-659 raises the maximum landing mass from the baseline 1805 kg to 1999 kg.

question: What is the maximum load permitted in the nose baggage compartment?
explanation: AFM 2.7 gives 30 kg for the nose baggage compartment, versus 45 kg for the cabin baggage compartment.

question: What is the combined maximum load for the cabin baggage compartment and baggage extension together?
explanation: AFM 2.7: the cabin compartment alone is 45 kg, the extension alone 18 kg, but the two together are still capped at 45 kg combined.

question: By how much may the ramp (taxi) mass exceed the maximum take-off mass, in a country where a flight begins at engine start?
explanation: A note under AFM 2.7 permits a ramp mass of MTOM + 8 kg (MTOM + 18 lb) in such countries, provided the mass at lift-off does not exceed the maximum take-off mass.

question: What is the maximum operating altitude of the DA 42 NG?
explanation: AFM 2.11 sets the maximum operating altitude at 18,000 ft (5,486 m) pressure altitude.

question: What is the minimum flight crew, and the maximum number of occupants?
explanation: AFM 2.12 requires a minimum crew of 1 and permits a maximum of 4 occupants.

question: What is the maximum bank angle permitted for approved maneuvers such as steep turns, Lazy Eights or Chandelles?
explanation: AFM 2.9 permits these maneuvers only up to a bank angle of 60°; more than 60° of bank is not approved in the Normal Category.

question: Is stalling with asymmetric power or one engine inoperative approved?

options.text: Yes, but only above 5,000 ft AGL
Yes, but only with flaps in the APP position
No, it is not permitted in the Normal Category

explanation: A caution under AFM 2.9 states that stalling with asymmetric power or one engine inoperative is not permitted.

question: What is the positive maneuvering load factor at vO and vNE (flaps UP)?
explanation: AFM 2.10 gives +3.8 as the positive load factor at vO and vNE; with flaps in APP or LDG it drops to +2.0.

question: What is the positive maneuvering load factor with flaps in the APP or LDG position?
explanation: AFM 2.10: with flaps extended the positive load factor limit is reduced to 2.0, versus 3.8 with flaps up.

question: What is the negative maneuvering load factor at vO and vNE?
explanation: AFM 2.10 gives -1.52 as the negative load factor limit at vO and vNE (clean); it is 0.0 with flaps in APP or LDG.

question: Are intentional negative-g maneuvers permitted?

options.text: Yes, but only with flaps UP

explanation: AFM 2.9 and 2.10 both carry a caution that intentional negative-g maneuvers are not permitted.

question: What is the usable fuel quantity in each main tank?
explanation: AFM 2.14: total fuel per main tank is 26.0 US gal, of which 25.0 US gal is usable — 1 US gal is unusable.

question: What is the usable fuel quantity in each auxiliary tank, if installed?
explanation: AFM 2.14: each auxiliary tank holds 13.7 US gal total, of which 13.2 US gal is usable.

question: What is the maximum permissible fuel quantity difference between the LH and RH main tanks?
explanation: AFM 2.14 lists the maximum permissible LH/RH difference as 5.0 US gal (18.9 liters).

question: What is the total usable fuel capacity per side with auxiliary tanks installed?
explanation: AFM 2.14: usable fuel per side totals 38.2 US gal (25.0 main + 13.2 auxiliary); total fuel (including unusable) per side is 39.7 US gal.

question: Which fuel additive is approved for anti-icing use, and what is its maximum concentration?
explanation: AFM 2.14 approves PRIST Hi-Flash as an anti-icing additive up to 1500 ppm, and only with JET A, JET A-1 or JP-8 fuel.

question: What is the maximum concentration of BIOBOR JF for initial fuel system treatment?
explanation: AFM 2.14: BIOBOR JF is limited to 270 ppm for initial treatment, dropping to 135 ppm for permanent use afterward.

question: Is it permitted to operate both engines with both FUEL SELECTORs in CROSSFEED at the same time, other than briefly for a ground test?

options.text: Yes, but only during single-engine training
Yes, this is the normal cruise configuration

explanation: AFM 2.14/4A.6.5 prohibits operating both engines with both fuel selectors in CROSSFEED, other than the brief 30-second ground test of the crossfeed function.

question: What must never be exceeded for autopilot operation — the maximum airspeed?
explanation: AFM 2.16.7 gives the autopilot's maximum operating airspeed as 180 KIAS, and its minimum as 90 KIAS.

question: What is the minimum airspeed for autopilot operation?
explanation: AFM 2.16.7 sets the minimum autopilot operating airspeed at 90 KIAS, with a maximum of 180 KIAS.

question: Below what altitude AGL are altitude-select captures prohibited?
explanation: AFM 2.16.7 item 7 prohibits altitude-select captures below 1200 ft AGL.

question: Below what altitude must the autopilot be disengaged during approach or departure?
explanation: AFM 2.16.7 requires autopilot disengagement below 200 ft AGL during approach and departure, and below 800 ft AGL for all other phases of flight.

question: Below what altitude must the autopilot be disengaged during phases of flight other than approach or departure?
explanation: AFM 2.16.7 requires the autopilot to be disengaged below 800 ft AGL for cruise, climb, descent and maneuvering; the limit is lower, at 200 ft AGL, for approach and departure.

question: Must the autopilot and yaw damper be disconnected during single-engine operation?

options.text: Yes — the autopilot and yaw damper must be disconnected during single engine operation
No — the autopilot may remain engaged to reduce pilot workload
Only the yaw damper must be disconnected, the autopilot may stay on
Only if the airspeed exceeds vMCA by more than 10 KIAS

explanation: AFM 2.16.7 item 2 requires the autopilot and yaw damper to be disconnected during take-off, landing and single-engine operation.

question: What kind of ILS approaches may be flown using the GFC 700 autopilot / flight director?
explanation: AFM 2.16.7 item 5 limits GFC700/flight-director ILS approaches to Category I only.

question: Is the DA 42 NG's G1000 approved for GPS WAAS operations such as LPV approaches?

options.text: Yes, for all GPS WAAS approach types
Only if MÄM 42-978 (G1000 NXi) is installed
No — the G1000 is not approved for WAAS operations
Yes, for LPV and LNAV/VNAV approaches only

explanation: AFM 2.16.6 item 8 states the G1000 is NOT approved for GPS WAAS operations, and SBAS functionality must be disabled on the GPS status page.

question: What is the minimum safe distance from a transmitting Garmin GWX 68 weather radar?
explanation: AFM 2.16.11 gives a minimum safe distance of 2.8 m for the GWX 68 and 2.3 m for the GWX 70; the radar must never be operated on the ground or in a hangar.

question: Is it permitted to take off on a Night VFR or IFR flight with an empty battery, even using external power to start the engines?

options.text: No — this is not permitted for either scenario
Yes, provided both engines are started from external power
Yes, provided the flight remains under 30 minutes
Yes, but only for Night VFR, never IFR

explanation: AFM 2.16.2 prohibits taking off for a Night VFR or IFR flight with an empty battery, and also prohibits using external power to start with an empty battery if the subsequent flight is Night VFR or IFR.

question: On what surfaces has take-off and landing been demonstrated?

options.text: Hard paved, grass, and soft/unprepared surfaces
Hard paved surfaces and grass runways

explanation: AFM 2.16.9 states take-off and landing has been demonstrated on hard paved surfaces (asphalt, concrete) and grass runways.
